exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.description: A flat barbell press for the chest, front delts and triceps, and the main upper-body strength lift.
howTo: Lie with your eyes under the bar and your feet flat. Pull your shoulder blades back and down.
Grip a little wider than your shoulders and unrack the bar over your shoulders.
Lower it under control to your mid-chest, with your elbows about 45–70° from your body.
Press back up and slightly back toward your face until your arms are straight.
exercises.tip: Keep your shoulder blades pinned and your butt on the bench the whole time.

exercises.name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
exercises.description: A barbell press on a 30–45° bench that shifts work toward the upper chest.
howTo: Set the bench at 30–45° and sit with your eyes just in front of the bar.
Pull your shoulder blades back and grip a little wider than your shoulders.
Lower the bar to your upper chest, just below your collarbones.
Press up until your arms are straight over your shoulders.
exercises.tip: A lower incline (around 30°) keeps more of the work on the chest instead of the shoulders.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.description: A flat press with dumbbells that gives a deeper chest stretch than a barbell.
howTo: Sit with the dumbbells on your thighs, then lie back and bring them to your chest.
Pull your shoulder blades back and plant your feet.
Press up and slightly in until your arms are straight, without banging the dumbbells together.
Lower slowly until you feel a stretch across your chest.
exercises.tip: Use the full range. The deep stretch at the bottom is the main reason to choose dumbbells.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
exercises.description: A dumbbell press on a 30–45° bench for the upper chest, with a long stretch at the bottom.
howTo: Set the bench at 30–45° and kick the dumbbells up to your shoulders as you lie back.
Pull your shoulder blades back and keep your chest up.
Press up until your arms are straight above your upper chest.
Lower slowly until your elbows are a little below the bench.
exercises.tip: Keep your wrists stacked over your elbows.

exercises.name: Machine Chest Press
exercises.description: A seated machine press that lets you push your chest hard without having to balance a weight.
howTo: Set the seat so the handles line up with your mid-chest.
Pull your shoulder blades back against the pad and grip the handles.
Press forward until your arms are almost straight.
Return slowly until you feel a stretch in your chest.
exercises.tip: Don't let your shoulders roll forward at the end of the press.

exercises.name: Weighted Dip
exercises.description: A bodyweight press on parallel bars, adding weight once bodyweight reps get easy, for the lower chest and triceps.
howTo: Support yourself on the bars with your arms straight, adding a belt or dumbbell if needed.
Lean your torso forward slightly to work the chest more.
Lower until your shoulders are a little below your elbows, or as low as feels comfortable.
Press back up to straight arms.
exercises.tip: Stop the descent at a depth your shoulders handle comfortably, and add depth over time.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.description: A bodyweight press from the floor for the chest, front delts and triceps, with some core work.
howTo: Put your hands a little wider than your shoulders and make a straight line from head to heels.
Brace your core and glutes.
Lower your chest to just above the floor, with your elbows about 45° from your body.
Push back up to straight arms.
exercises.tip: Keep your hips level, not sagging or piked up.

exercises.name: Cable Fly
exercises.description: A cable fly that keeps tension on the chest through a big stretch.
howTo: Set the pulleys at chest height or a little higher and take one handle in each hand.
Step forward into a staggered stance, with a slight bend in your elbows.
Bring your hands together in front of your chest in a wide hugging arc.
Open back out slowly until you feel a stretch in your chest.
exercises.tip: Keep the elbow bend fixed. This is a hug, not a press.

exercises.name: Pec Deck
exercises.description: A machine fly for the chest that's easy to control and push close to failure.
howTo: Set the seat so the handles are at chest height when you hold them.
Sit tall with your shoulder blades back.
Bring the handles together in front of you.
Let them open slowly until you feel a stretch in your chest.
exercises.tip: Don't let your shoulders shrug forward as the handles meet.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Fly
exercises.description: A fly with dumbbells on a flat bench that stretches the chest hard at the bottom.
howTo: Lie on a bench with the dumbbells over your chest and your palms facing each other.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows and lower the weights out to the sides in an arc.
Stop when you feel a strong chest stretch, usually with your upper arms about level with the bench.
Bring them back up along the same arc.
exercises.tip: Go lighter than you think. The stretch at the bottom is where your shoulders are most exposed.

exercises.name: Overhead Press
exercises.description: A standing barbell press overhead for the front delts and triceps, with core and upper-trap work.
howTo: Start with the bar on your front shoulders, your hands just outside shoulder width, and your glutes and abs tight.
Press straight up, moving your head back slightly so the bar can pass.
Finish with the bar over your mid-foot and your head through between your arms.
Lower under control back to your shoulders.
exercises.tip: Squeeze your glutes so you don't lean back into the lift.

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press
exercises.description: A seated dumbbell press for the front and side delts, with back support.
howTo: Set the bench upright or nearly upright and bring the dumbbells to shoulder height.
Keep your back against the pad and your feet planted.
Press up until your arms are straight, without letting the weights touch.
Lower to about ear level or a little below.
exercises.tip: Keep your forearms vertical under the weights.

exercises.name: Machine Shoulder Press
exercises.description: A machine overhead press that loads the delts without having to balance a weight.
howTo: Adjust the seat so the handles start at about shoulder height.
Sit back against the pad and grip the handles.
Press up until your arms are almost straight.
Lower slowly to the start position.
exercises.tip: Don't arch your lower back off the pad.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
exercises.description: A side raise with dumbbells, the go-to exercise for the side delts.
howTo: Stand with the dumbbells at your sides and a slight bend in your elbows.
Lean a little forward and raise your arms out to the sides.
Stop at about shoulder height, leading with your elbows.
Lower slowly.
exercises.tip: Think 'push the weights out' rather than 'up' so your traps stay out of it.

exercises.name: Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.description: A one-arm cable side raise that keeps the side delt loaded at the bottom, where dumbbells go slack.
howTo: Set the pulley low and stand side-on to it, holding the handle with your far hand.
Let the cable pull your hand across your body slightly.
Raise your arm out to the side to about shoulder height.
Lower slowly back across your body.
exercises.tip: Standing a little in front of the pulley gives a longer stretch.

exercises.name: Upright Row
exercises.description: A barbell or cable pull up the front of the body for the side delts and upper traps.
howTo: Hold the bar with your hands about shoulder width apart, or wider.
Pull it up close to your body, leading with your elbows.
Stop when your elbows are about shoulder height.
Lower under control.
exercises.tip: A wider grip and stopping at shoulder height are usually easiest on the shoulders.

exercises.name: Reverse Pec Deck
exercises.description: A machine reverse fly for the rear delts and mid upper back.
howTo: Sit facing the pad with the handles at shoulder height.
Hold the handles with a slight bend in your elbows.
Sweep your arms back and out until they're in line with your body.
Return slowly.
exercises.tip: Move at the shoulder and don't squeeze your shoulder blades too hard, to keep the work on the rear delts.

exercises.name: Face Pull
exercises.description: A rope cable pull to the face for the rear delts and mid traps.
howTo: Set the pulley at upper-chest to face height and grip the rope.
Step back until the cable is tight.
Pull the rope toward your face and split the ends apart, with your elbows high.
Return slowly.
exercises.tip: Finish with your hands beside your ears and your elbows out.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Rear Delt Fly
exercises.description: A bent-over reverse fly with dumbbells for the rear delts.
howTo: Hinge forward at the hips until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor, with the dumbbells hanging down.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise your arms out to the sides until they're about level with your back.
Lower slowly.
exercises.tip: Use light weights and keep your shoulders away from your ears.

exercises.name: Front Raise
exercises.description: A forward raise with a dumbbell or plate for the front delts.
howTo: Stand with the weights in front of your thighs.
Raise your arms forward to about shoulder height.
Pause briefly.
Lower slowly.
exercises.tip: Most pressing already works the front delts, so treat this as optional.

exercises.name: Pull-Up
exercises.description: A bodyweight pull-up with an overhand grip, the main lift for the lats.
howTo: Hang from the bar with your hands a little wider than your shoulders and your palms facing away.
Pull your shoulders down, then drive your elbows toward your hips.
Pull until your chin clears the bar.
Lower all the way to a full hang.
exercises.tip: Use the full range. The dead hang at the bottom is the stretch that builds the lats.

exercises.name: Chin-Up
exercises.description: An underhand pull-up that uses more biceps.
howTo: Hang with your palms facing you, about shoulder width apart.
Pull your shoulders down and drive your elbows down to your sides.
Pull until your chin clears the bar.
Lower all the way to a full hang.
exercises.tip: Avoid kicking or swinging. Keep it a strict pull.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown
exercises.description: A cable pulldown that works like a pull-up with adjustable weight.
howTo: Set the thigh pad snug and grip the bar a little wider than your shoulders.
Lean back slightly with your chest up.
Pull the bar to your upper chest, driving your elbows down.
Let it rise slowly until your arms are straight and your lats stretch.
exercises.tip: Don't yank with your lower back. Pull from your elbows.

exercises.name: Close-Grip Pulldown
exercises.description: A pulldown with a narrow, palms-facing grip that gives a long lat stretch and works the biceps more.
howTo: Attach a close-grip handle and sit with your thighs locked under the pad.
Lean back slightly.
Pull the handle to your upper chest, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Return until your arms are straight.
exercises.tip: Let your shoulders rise at the top to get the full stretch.

exercises.name: Barbell Row
exercises.description: A bent-over barbell row for the upper back and lats, which also makes the lower back work to hold the position.
howTo: Hinge forward to about 30–45° from the floor, holding the bar at arm's length.
Brace your core and keep your back flat.
Row the bar to your lower ribs.
Lower it under control without standing up.
exercises.tip: Keep your torso angle the same on every rep. If it changes, the weight is too heavy.

exercises.name: Pendlay Row
exercises.description: A strict barbell row from the floor, with the torso close to parallel, for the upper back and lats.
howTo: Set up with your torso nearly parallel to the floor and the bar on the ground.
Grip slightly wider than your shoulders and brace.
Pull the bar explosively to your lower chest.
Set it back on the floor and reset before the next rep.
exercises.tip: Don't let your back round as you pull.

exercises.name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
exercises.description: A one-arm dumbbell row with a hand on a bench for support, which allows a long stretch for the lats.
howTo: Put one hand and knee on a bench, with the dumbbell in your other hand.
Let the weight hang so your shoulder stretches forward.
Row it toward your hip, keeping your elbow close.
Lower slowly back to the full stretch.
exercises.tip: Pull toward your hip, not your armpit, to keep the work on the lats.

exercises.name: Chest-Supported Row
exercises.description: A row with your chest on a pad, so your lower back stays out of it and the upper back does the work.
howTo: Lie face-down on an incline bench or row machine pad.
Let the weights or handles hang at arm's length.
Row your elbows back until your upper arms are level with your torso.
Lower slowly.
exercises.tip: Keep your chest on the pad. Lifting off turns it into a cheat row.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.description: A seated cable row for the upper back and lats.
howTo: Sit with your feet on the platform and your knees slightly bent, holding the handle.
Sit tall and let your arms stretch forward.
Pull the handle to your stomach, bringing your shoulder blades back.
Return slowly until your arms are straight.
exercises.tip: Keep your torso nearly still, with only a small lean, and let your arms do the moving.

exercises.name: T-Bar Row
exercises.description: A landmine or machine row, done hinged over with a handle, for upper-back thickness.
howTo: Stand over the bar with your hips hinged and your back flat, gripping the handle.
Brace your core.
Row the handle toward your chest.
Lower under control.
exercises.tip: Hold your hip hinge. Don't let your torso stand up as you pull.

exercises.name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
exercises.description: A cable pulldown with straight arms, so the lats work without the biceps.
howTo: Face a high pulley holding a bar or rope, with your arms straight.
Hinge slightly at the hips.
Sweep your arms down to your thighs, keeping your elbows nearly locked.
Let them rise slowly until your lats stretch.
exercises.tip: Think about pulling with your armpits, not your hands.

exercises.name: Barbell Shrug
exercises.description: A barbell shrug for the upper traps.
howTo: Hold the bar at arm's length in front of your thighs.
Lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears.
Pause at the top.
Lower all the way down.
exercises.tip: Go straight up and down. There's no need to roll your shoulders.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Shrug
exercises.description: A dumbbell shrug for the upper traps, with your hands at your sides.
howTo: Hold the dumbbells at your sides.
Lift your shoulders straight up.
Pause at the top.
Lower until you feel a stretch.
exercises.tip: Use straps if your grip gives out before your traps.

exercises.name: Barbell Curl
exercises.description: A standing barbell curl for the biceps.
howTo: Hold the bar with an underhand, shoulder-width grip.
Keep your elbows at your sides.
Curl the bar up to shoulder height.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.
exercises.tip: Don't swing. If your hips move, the weight is too heavy.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Curl
exercises.description: A standing or seated dumbbell curl for the biceps.
howTo: Hold the dumbbells at your sides with your palms forward.
Keep your elbows fixed and curl the weights up.
Squeeze at the top.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.
exercises.tip: Rotate your pinky up slightly at the top for a harder biceps contraction.

exercises.name: Hammer Curl
exercises.description: A curl with your palms facing each other, for the brachialis, the forearm and the biceps.
howTo: Hold the dumbbells at your sides with your palms facing in.
Keep your elbows at your sides.
Curl the weights up, keeping the neutral grip.
Lower slowly.
exercises.tip: Keep your wrists straight and in line with your forearms.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
exercises.description: A curl lying back on an incline bench so the biceps work from a long stretch.
howTo: Set the bench at 45–60° and lie back with your arms hanging straight down.
Keep your upper arms still, pointing at the floor.
Curl the dumbbells up.
Lower all the way until your arms are fully straight.
exercises.tip: Let your arms hang behind your body. That stretch is what makes this curl work.

exercises.name: Preacher Curl
exercises.description: A curl with your upper arms resting on an angled pad, which removes all body swing.
howTo: Sit at the preacher bench with your armpits snug against the pad.
Hold an EZ bar or dumbbells with your arms almost straight.
Curl up until your forearms are near vertical.
Lower slowly to almost straight.
exercises.tip: Control the bottom of each rep. Don't drop into it.

exercises.name: Cable Curl
exercises.description: A cable curl that keeps the biceps under steady tension.
howTo: Face a low pulley holding a straight bar or rope.
Keep your elbows at your sides.
Curl up to your shoulders.
Lower slowly.
exercises.tip: Step back a little so the cable pulls through the whole rep.

exercises.name: Close-Grip Bench Press
exercises.description: A bench press with a narrower grip that works the triceps harder.
howTo: Lie on the bench and grip the bar about shoulder width apart.
Pull your shoulder blades back.
Lower the bar to your lower chest, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Press until your arms are straight.
exercises.tip: Shoulder width is close enough. A grip that's too narrow just strains your wrists.

exercises.name: Skull Crusher
exercises.description: A lying triceps extension with an EZ bar or dumbbells.
howTo: Lie on a bench holding the weight over your shoulders.
Tilt your upper arms back slightly toward your head.
Bend your elbows to lower the weight behind your head or to your forehead.
Straighten your arms back to the start.
exercises.tip: Lowering behind your head gives the long head more stretch.

exercises.name: Triceps Pushdown
exercises.description: A cable pushdown for the triceps.
howTo: Face a high pulley holding a bar or rope.
Pin your elbows to your sides.
Push down until your arms are straight.
Let it rise slowly until your forearms pass parallel to the floor.
exercises.tip: Keep your elbows still. Only your forearms should move.

exercises.name: Overhead Cable Triceps Extension
exercises.description: A cable triceps extension with your arms overhead, which loads the long head at a stretch.
howTo: Face away from a pulley, holding a rope behind your head with your arms overhead.
Stagger your stance and brace your core.
Straighten your arms forward and up.
Let the rope come back slowly behind your head.
exercises.tip: Get a deep stretch at the bottom of every rep.

exercises.name: Wrist Curl
exercises.description: A forearm curl for the wrist flexors.
howTo: Rest your forearms on a bench or your thighs, with your palms up and your wrists past the edge.
Let the weight roll down to your fingers.
Curl your wrists up as far as they go.
Lower slowly.
exercises.tip: Use high reps and a full range.

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.description: A barbell back squat for the quads, glutes and adductors, and the main lower-body strength lift.
howTo: Set the bar on your upper back, step out and stand with your feet about shoulder width apart and your toes slightly out.
Brace your core and sit down between your hips, with your knees tracking over your toes.
Go as deep as you can while keeping your back neutral, ideally with your hip crease below your knee.
Drive back up through your mid-foot.
exercises.tip: Depth matters. Deep squats build more quad and glute than half reps.

exercises.name: Front Squat
exercises.description: A barbell squat with the bar on the front of the shoulders, so your torso stays upright and the quads do more.
howTo: Rest the bar on your front shoulders, with your elbows high in a clean grip or with crossed arms.
Brace hard and keep your chest up.
Squat down as deep as you can while staying upright.
Stand back up, leading with your elbows.
exercises.tip: If your elbows drop, the bar will roll forward.

exercises.name: Hack Squat
exercises.description: A machine squat on an angled sled, for the quads, with your back supported.
howTo: Put your back against the pad and your feet at mid-platform, about shoulder width apart.
Release the safeties.
Lower until your knees are deeply bent.
Press back up without locking out hard.
exercises.tip: Lower foot placement works the quads more. Higher placement works the glutes more.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.description: A machine press for the quads and glutes, with no balance or lower-back demand.
howTo: Sit with your back flat against the pad and your feet about shoulder width apart on the platform.
Release the safeties.
Lower until your knees are deeply bent, without letting your lower back peel off the pad.
Press back up.
exercises.tip: Stop the descent before your hips curl up off the seat.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.description: A one-leg squat with your rear foot up on a bench, for the quads and glutes.
howTo: Stand in front of a bench with the top of your rear foot resting on it.
Lower straight down until your rear knee nearly touches the floor.
Keep your front foot flat and your knee tracking over your toes.
Drive up through your front foot.
exercises.tip: A longer stride and leaning forward work the glutes more. A shorter stride and staying upright work the quads more.

exercises.name: Walking Lunge
exercises.description: Alternating forward lunges as you walk, for the quads and glutes.
howTo: Hold dumbbells at your sides and step forward into a long stride.
Lower until your back knee nearly touches the floor.
Push through your front foot and step straight into the next lunge.
Keep your torso tall.
exercises.tip: Take controlled steps. Don't let your front knee cave inward.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.description: A machine knee extension, the best exercise for isolating the quads, including the rectus femoris.
howTo: Adjust the seat so your knees line up with the machine's pivot point.
Hook the pad just above your ankles.
Straighten your legs fully.
Lower slowly until your knees are bent past 90°.
exercises.tip: Leaning back slightly stretches the rectus femoris more.

exercises.name: Deadlift
exercises.description: A conventional deadlift from the floor, a full-body pull for the posterior chain, meaning the hamstrings, glutes and back.
howTo: Stand with the bar over your mid-foot and your feet about hip width apart.
Hinge down and grip the bar just outside your legs, with your back flat and your shoulders over the bar.
Push the floor away and stand up with the bar sliding up your legs.
Lower it back down the same way.
exercises.tip: Keep the bar touching your legs the whole time.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
exercises.description: A hip hinge that lowers the bar down your legs with soft knees, putting a long stretch on the hamstrings.
howTo: Stand tall holding the bar at your hips, with your knees slightly bent.
Push your hips back and let the bar slide down your thighs, keeping your back flat.
Go down until you feel a strong hamstring stretch, usually around mid-shin.
Drive your hips forward to stand back up.
exercises.tip: The movement is hips back, not bending down. Your knee angle barely changes.

exercises.name: Stiff-Leg Dumbbell Deadlift
exercises.description: A dumbbell hinge with straighter legs, for the hamstrings.
howTo: Hold the dumbbells in front of your thighs.
Keep your legs nearly straight and push your hips back.
Lower the weights along your legs until your hamstrings are stretched.
Squeeze your glutes and stand up.
exercises.tip: Keep your back flat. Only go as low as your hamstrings allow.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust
exercises.description: A barbell hip thrust with your upper back on a bench, for the glutes.
howTo: Sit with your upper back against a bench and a padded bar across your hips.
Plant your feet so your shins are vertical at the top.
Drive through your heels and lift your hips until your body is flat from shoulders to knees.
Lower under control.
exercises.tip: Tuck your chin and ribs down so your lower back doesn't arch at the top.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl
exercises.description: A machine leg curl lying face-down, for the hamstrings.
howTo: Lie face-down with the pad just above your heels and your knees just off the bench edge.
Curl your heels toward your glutes.
Squeeze at the top.
Lower slowly until your legs are straight.
exercises.tip: Keep your hips pressed down into the pad.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
exercises.description: A seated machine leg curl. Your hips are bent, so the hamstrings work from a longer stretch.
howTo: Sit with your knees lined up with the pivot, the pad behind your lower legs, and the thigh pad snug.
Lean your torso forward slightly.
Curl your heels down and back.
Return slowly until your legs are straight.
exercises.tip: Leaning forward adds stretch. Research suggests seated curls build more than lying curls.

exercises.name: Back Extension
exercises.description: A hip extension on a 45° or horizontal bench, for the lower back, glutes and hamstrings.
howTo: Set the pad just below your hip bones and lock your heels in.
Lower your torso forward.
Raise up until your body is in a straight line.
Lower slowly.
exercises.tip: Round your upper back slightly to work the glutes more, or keep it flat to work the lower back.

exercises.name: Hip Adduction Machine
exercises.description: A seated machine that squeezes the legs together, for the inner-thigh adductors.
howTo: Sit with the pads on the inside of your knees and set the start width so you feel a stretch.
Squeeze your legs together.
Pause briefly.
Open back out slowly.
exercises.tip: Leaning forward slightly lets the adductors work through a longer range.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
exercises.description: A calf raise with straight knees, for the gastrocnemius.
howTo: Stand on a step or calf machine with the balls of your feet on the edge.
Let your heels drop for a deep stretch and pause there.
Rise up as high as you can.
Lower slowly back to the stretch.
exercises.tip: Pause in the bottom stretch for a second. Bouncing skips most of the benefit.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise
exercises.description: A calf raise with bent knees, which shifts work to the soleus.
howTo: Sit with the pad on your lower thighs and the balls of your feet on the platform.
Drop your heels into a deep stretch.
Raise your heels as high as you can.
Lower slowly.
exercises.tip: Use a full range and steady reps, without bouncing.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.description: A hanging raise of the legs or knees for the abs.
howTo: Hang from a bar with your arms straight.
Tilt your pelvis back and raise your knees or straight legs.
Curl your hips up toward your chest.
Lower slowly without swinging.
exercises.tip: Curling your pelvis up is what works the abs. Just lifting your legs mostly works the hip flexors.

exercises.name: Cable Crunch
exercises.description: A kneeling crunch against a cable, for the abs.
howTo: Kneel facing a high pulley, holding a rope beside your head.
Keep your hips still.
Curl your ribs toward your pelvis, rounding your spine.
Return slowly to a stretch.
exercises.tip: Move your spine, not your hips. Your butt shouldn't sit back.

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
exercises.description: A rollout on an ab wheel that makes the abs resist arching, with a big stretch.
howTo: Kneel holding the wheel under your shoulders.
Brace your core and tuck your pelvis slightly.
Roll forward as far as you can without your lower back sagging.
Pull back to the start using your abs.
exercises.tip: Start with short rollouts and lengthen them over time.

exercises.name: Hip Abduction Machine
exercises.description: A seated machine that pushes the legs apart, for the glute medius, glute minimus and TFL.
howTo: Sit with the pads on the outside of your knees.
Push your knees out as far as you can.
Pause briefly.
Return slowly.
exercises.tip: Leaning forward slightly works the glute medius more.

exercises.name: Cable Hip Abduction
exercises.description: A standing cable leg raise out to the side, for the glute medius.
howTo: Attach an ankle cuff on a low pulley and stand side-on with the cuffed leg away from the machine.
Hold the machine for balance.
Raise your leg out to the side without leaning.
Lower slowly.
exercises.tip: Keep your toes pointing forward. Rotating them up shifts the work to the hip flexors.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Hip Abduction
exercises.description: A side-lying leg raise for the glute medius. It needs no equipment.
howTo: Lie on your side with your legs stacked and straight.
Rotate your top leg's toes slightly down.
Raise your top leg to about 30–45°.
Lower slowly.
exercises.tip: Keep your hips stacked. Don't roll back.

exercises.name: Banded Lateral Walk
exercises.description: Side steps with a resistance band around the legs, for the glute medius.
howTo: Put a band above your knees or around your ankles and sink into a quarter squat.
Step sideways, keeping tension on the band.
Bring your trailing foot in without letting your feet touch.
Take the same number of steps in each direction.
exercises.tip: Stay low and keep your knees pushed out the whole time.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Step-Up
exercises.description: A one-leg step up onto a box or bench, for the quads and glutes.
howTo: Hold dumbbells and put one foot flat on a knee-height box.
Lean forward slightly and drive through the top foot.
Stand fully on the box without pushing off your back foot.
Step down slowly.
exercises.tip: Let the top leg do the work, not a bounce off the floor.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Squat
exercises.description: A squat on a fixed bar path. It loads the quads hard with less balance and lower-back demand than a free-bar squat.
howTo: Set the bar on your upper back and unhook it with a twist of the wrists.
Place your feet slightly in front of the bar, about shoulder width apart.
Sit down with your knees tracking over your toes until your hips are below your knees.
Drive back up and re-hook the bar at the top.
exercises.tip: Feet a little forward shifts work toward the quads and keeps your knees comfortable.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Bench Press
exercises.description: A flat press on a fixed bar path. It's easy to push close to failure safely without a spotter.
howTo: Set the bench so the bar lines up with your mid-chest.
Grip just wider than shoulder width and unhook the bar.
Lower it under control to your mid-chest.
Press back up and re-hook at the top.
exercises.tip: Use the safety stops so you can take sets close to failure alone.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Incline Press
exercises.description: An incline press on a fixed bar path that biases the upper chest.
howTo: Set the bench to about 30 degrees, with the bar over your upper chest.
Grip just wider than shoulder width and unhook the bar.
Lower it to just below your collarbones.
Press back up and re-hook at the top.
exercises.tip: A low incline of 30 degrees keeps the upper chest working and the front delts from taking over.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Overhead Press
exercises.description: A seated or standing shoulder press on a fixed bar path for the front and side delts.
howTo: Sit on an upright bench with the bar just in front of your face.
Grip about shoulder width and unhook the bar.
Lower it to about chin height.
Press up until your arms are straight, then lower under control.
exercises.tip: Sitting with back support lets you load the delts without bracing hard.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Row
exercises.description: A bent-over row on a fixed bar path for the lats and upper back.
howTo: Set the bar at about knee height and grip just outside your legs.
Hinge forward until your torso is about 45 degrees or lower.
Pull the bar to your lower ribs, leading with your elbows.
Lower under control without letting your back round.
exercises.tip: Pause with the bar touching your body to stop momentum taking over.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Romanian Deadlift
exercises.description: A hip hinge on a fixed bar path that stretches and loads the hamstrings and glutes.
howTo: Stand with the bar at your thighs and your feet hip width apart.
Soften your knees and push your hips back, keeping the bar against your legs.
Lower until you feel a deep hamstring stretch, usually just below the knee.
Drive your hips forward to stand back up.
exercises.tip: Hips back, not down. Stop where your back would start to round.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Split Squat
exercises.description: A single-leg squat on a fixed bar path for the quads and glutes, with less balance demand.
howTo: Set the bar on your upper back and step one foot forward and one back.
Lower straight down until your back knee nearly touches the floor.
Keep most of your weight on the front foot.
Drive up through the front foot, finish all reps, then switch sides.
exercises.tip: A longer stride shifts work to the glutes, and a shorter one to the quads.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Calf Raise
exercises.description: A standing calf raise with the bar on your back, done on a step for full range.
howTo: Set the bar on your upper back and stand with the balls of your feet on a step or plate.
Lower your heels as far as you can and pause in the stretch.
Rise as high as you can onto your toes.
Repeat under control without bouncing.
exercises.tip: Pause for a second at the bottom. The stretch is where calves grow most.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Hip Thrust
exercises.description: A hip thrust on a fixed bar path, which is easier to set up than with a barbell.
howTo: Sit with your upper back against a bench and the padded bar across your hips.
Plant your feet flat, about hip width apart.
Drive your hips up until your body is straight from knees to shoulders.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower under control.
exercises.tip: Keep your chin tucked and ribs down so the glutes, not your lower back, finish the rep.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Shrug
exercises.description: A shrug on a fixed bar path for the upper traps.
howTo: Stand holding the bar at arm's length, hands just outside your thighs.
Lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears.
Pause at the top.
Lower all the way down for a full stretch.
exercises.tip: Straight up and down. Rolling your shoulders adds nothing.

exercises.name: Incline-Bench Cable Pullover
exercises.description: A lat isolation done lying on an incline bench, pulling a cable from behind your head down to your hips, so the lats are loaded hard at full stretch.
howTo: Set an incline bench with its head end facing a low cable, and take a rope or straight bar with your arms overhead.
Lie back with a slight elbow bend and let the cable pull your arms back until your lats are stretched.
Sweep the handle down in an arc to your hips, driving with your elbows.
Return slowly to the full stretch.
exercises.tip: Keep the elbow angle fixed. If your elbows bend and straighten, it turns into a triceps press.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Pullover
exercises.description: A dumbbell pullover across a flat bench that works the lats and chest in a long, stretched position.
howTo: Lie on a bench holding one dumbbell over your chest with both hands.
Keeping a slight elbow bend, lower the weight back behind your head until you feel a stretch in your lats and chest.
Pull it back over your chest in the same arc.
exercises.tip: Tension drops off at the top, so stop just before the weight is over your face.

exercises.name: Pullover Machine
exercises.description: A machine pullover that loads the lats evenly from full stretch to the hips, with no balancing.
howTo: Set the seat so your shoulders line up with the machine's pivot, and put your elbows on the pads.
Let the pads go back overhead until your lats are stretched.
Drive your elbows down to your sides, then return slowly.
exercises.tip: Push through your elbows, not your hands.

exercises.name: Chest-Supported T-Bar Row
exercises.description: A chest-supported T-bar row that lets you row heavy without the lower back holding you up.
howTo: Lie face down on the pad and take the handles with your arms straight.
Pull the handles toward your lower chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause briefly, then lower until your arms are straight and your shoulder blades spread.
exercises.tip: Let the shoulder blades move. Full reach at the bottom is part of the rep.

exercises.name: Landmine Viking Press
exercises.description: A two-handed overhead press using a landmine with a Viking handle, on a forward arc that is easier on the shoulders than a strict press.
howTo: Stand facing the handle with your feet hip width apart and the grips at shoulder height.
Brace and press up and slightly forward until your arms are straight.
Lower back to your shoulders under control.
exercises.tip: Don't lean back to finish the rep. Ribs down, glutes tight.

exercises.name: One-Arm Landmine Press
exercises.description: A one-arm press up and forward along a landmine arc for the front delts and upper chest, and kind on cranky shoulders.
howTo: Stand in a split stance holding the end of the bar at your shoulder in one hand.
Press up and forward until your arm is straight, reaching a little at the top.
Lower back to your shoulder under control.
exercises.tip: Keep your hips square. Don't twist to get the bar up.

exercises.name: Two-Arm Landmine Press
exercises.description: A two-handed landmine press with interlocked hands, working the upper chest and front delts at a steep incline.
howTo: Hold the end of the bar at your chest with both hands cupped together.
Lean slightly into the bar and press it up and away until your arms are straight.
Lower it back to your chest under control.
exercises.tip: Press from the chest, not the legs. Keep the knees soft but still.

exercises.name: Meadows Row
exercises.description: A one-arm landmine row, done standing side-on to the bar, that gives the lats a long stretch at the bottom.
howTo: Stand side-on to the end of a landmine bar in a staggered stance and grip the thick end overhand.
Rest your free forearm on your front knee and let the bar hang so your lat stretches.
Row your elbow up and back toward your hip.
Lower slowly to the full stretch.
exercises.tip: Use straps if your grip gives out first. The bar end is thick.

exercises.name: Landmine Squat
exercises.description: A squat holding the end of a landmine bar at your chest, which lets you sit upright and deep with little load on the spine.
howTo: Hold the end of the bar at your chest with both hands and step back so you lean slightly into it.
Sit straight down between your hips, keeping your chest up.
Go as deep as you can control, then drive up through your mid-foot.
exercises.tip: Lean into the bar a little. It acts like a counterweight and helps you stay upright.

exercises.name: Landmine Romanian Deadlift
exercises.description: A hip hinge holding the end of a landmine bar, which loads the hamstrings and glutes on a forgiving arc.
howTo: Stand facing the bar end, hold it with both hands at arm's length, with soft knees.
Push your hips back and let the bar slide down your thighs until your hamstrings are stretched.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall.
exercises.tip: Reach your hips back, not your hands down.

exercises.name: Landmine Rotation
exercises.description: A loaded rotation that swings a landmine bar from hip to hip, training the obliques to make and resist rotation.
howTo: Hold the end of the bar overhead at arm's length with both hands, feet wider than your hips.
Rotate your torso and pivot your back foot to bring the bar down to one hip.
Reverse the arc through the top and down to the other side.
exercises.tip: Move from the ribcage and hips together. Keep the arms long.

exercises.name: Preacher Curl Machine
exercises.description: A machine preacher curl that keeps the biceps loaded right down to the stretched, arms-straight position.
howTo: Set the seat so your armpits sit at the top of the pad.
Curl the handles up until your forearms are vertical.
Lower all the way until your arms are nearly straight.
exercises.tip: The bottom half is the valuable part. Don't cut it short.

exercises.name: Seated Curl Machine
exercises.description: A selectorized biceps curl with a fixed path and steady resistance.
howTo: Sit with your elbows on the pad, lined up with the machine's pivot.
Curl the handles up fully.
Lower under control to almost straight.
exercises.tip: Keep your elbows planted. If they lift, the weight is too heavy.

exercises.name: Cable Rope Hammer Curl
exercises.description: A neutral-grip rope curl on a low cable for the brachialis, brachioradialis and biceps.
howTo: Stand facing a low cable holding a rope with palms facing each other.
Curl up, keeping your elbows by your sides.
Lower slowly to straight arms.
exercises.tip: Don't let your elbows drift forward at the top.

exercises.name: Bayesian Cable Curl
exercises.description: A one-arm cable curl facing away from a low pulley, with your arm behind your body, so the biceps are stretched at the bottom.
howTo: Set a cable low, take the handle and step forward until your arm is pulled behind you.
Curl up without letting your elbow swing forward.
Lower slowly until your arm is straight behind you.
exercises.tip: Stagger your stance and lean forward a little to keep the arm back.

exercises.name: High Cable Curl
exercises.description: A curl with both arms out to the sides from high pulleys, hitting the biceps in the shortened position.
howTo: Stand between two high pulleys holding a handle in each hand, arms out at shoulder height.
Curl your hands toward your ears, keeping your elbows high.
Straighten back out slowly.
exercises.tip: Keep your upper arms still. Only your forearms move.

exercises.name: Triceps Extension Machine
exercises.description: A seated machine triceps extension with your elbows on a pad, for steady, isolated triceps work.
howTo: Sit with your elbows on the pad, lined up with the pivot.
Extend the handles until your arms are straight.
Return slowly until your elbows are fully bent.
exercises.tip: Keep your shoulders down. Let the elbows do all the work.

exercises.name: Seated Dip Machine
exercises.description: A seated dip machine that trains the triceps and lower chest without supporting your body weight.
howTo: Sit tall and take the handles at your sides.
Press down until your arms are straight.
Let the handles come up slowly until your elbows are bent about 90 degrees.
exercises.tip: Stay upright for triceps. Lean forward a little for more chest.

exercises.name: Overhead Triceps Extension Machine
exercises.description: A machine triceps extension with your arms overhead, which stretches the long head of the triceps.
howTo: Sit with your upper arms overhead on the pad and grip the handles behind your head.
Extend your arms until they are straight.
Lower slowly until your elbows are fully bent.
exercises.tip: Keep your elbows pointed forward, not out to the sides.

exercises.name: Plate-Loaded Chest Press
exercises.description: A plate-loaded lever chest press, whose resistance curve feels heavier at the bottom than a selectorized stack.
howTo: Set the seat so the handles line up with your mid-chest.
Press the handles forward until your arms are nearly straight.
Bring them back slowly until you feel a stretch across your chest.
exercises.tip: Keep your shoulder blades pinned back against the pad.

exercises.name: Incline Chest Press Machine
exercises.description: A machine incline press that targets the upper chest along a fixed path.
howTo: Set the seat so the handles start at upper-chest height.
Press up and forward until your arms are nearly straight.
Lower slowly to a deep stretch.
exercises.tip: Keep your chest high and your shoulders down.

exercises.name: Decline Chest Press Machine
exercises.description: A machine decline press that biases the lower chest and is gentle on the shoulders.
howTo: Sit with the handles in line with your lower chest.
Press down and forward until your arms are nearly straight.
Return slowly to a full stretch.
exercises.tip: Think of driving your hands toward your hips.

exercises.name: Iso-Lateral Chest Press
exercises.description: A Hammer Strength style press with independent arms that converge toward the midline, so each side works on its own through a deep stretch.
howTo: Set the seat so the handles line up with your mid-chest.
Press both arms forward, letting them come together in front of you.
Lower slowly to a deep chest stretch.
exercises.tip: Press one arm at a time now and then to even out a weaker side.

exercises.name: Iso-Lateral Shoulder Press
exercises.description: A plate-loaded shoulder press with independent arms on a slightly forward path.
howTo: Set the seat so the handles start at about chin height.
Press up until your arms are nearly straight.
Lower until your hands are at about ear level.
exercises.tip: Keep your back on the pad. Don't arch to finish the rep.

exercises.name: Seated Lateral Raise Machine (Elbow Pads)
exercises.description: A seated machine lateral raise with pads on your outer arms, so your grip and traps barely help and the side delts do the lifting.
howTo: Sit with the machine pivot lined up with your shoulders and the pads against your outer upper arms.
Raise your arms out to the sides to shoulder height, pushing through the pads.
Lower slowly until the weight nearly touches down.
exercises.tip: Relax your hands. Pushing through your elbows keeps the traps out of it.

exercises.name: High Row Machine
exercises.description: A plate-loaded row that pulls down and back from overhead, a cross between a pulldown and a row.
howTo: Sit with your thighs under the pad and reach up for the handles.
Pull your elbows down and back toward your hips.
Let your arms go back up until your lats stretch.
exercises.tip: Drive the elbows, not the hands.

exercises.name: Low Row Machine
exercises.description: A plate-loaded seated row that pulls from low to your waist, mostly for the lats and mid-back.
howTo: Sit with your chest against the pad and take the low handles.
Pull your elbows back past your torso.
Let your arms go forward fully so your shoulder blades spread.
exercises.tip: Keep your chest on the pad the whole time.

exercises.name: Iso-Lateral Row
exercises.description: A chest-supported row with independent arms, so each side pulls its own weight.
howTo: Set the seat so the handles are at about chest height, with your chest on the pad.
Row one or both handles back until your elbows pass your torso.
Return slowly to a full reach.
exercises.tip: Try one arm at a time with a pause at the top.

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Lat Pulldown
exercises.description: A pulldown with a wide overhand grip, for the lats and upper back.
howTo: Grip the bar well outside shoulder width and sit with your thighs under the pad.
Pull the bar to your upper chest, driving your elbows down.
Let the bar go up until your arms are straight.
exercises.tip: Lean back only slightly. This isn't a row.

exercises.name: Neutral-Grip Lat Pulldown
exercises.description: A pulldown with palms facing each other, which lets most people pull hard with comfortable shoulders.
howTo: Take a neutral-grip handle and sit with your thighs under the pad.
Pull your hands to your upper chest, elbows driving down to your sides.
Return until your arms are straight and your lats stretch.
exercises.tip: Pull your elbows toward your back pockets.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Lat Pulldown
exercises.description: A one-arm pulldown that lets each lat work through a longer range than with a bar.
howTo: Kneel or sit under a high pulley and take one handle.
Pull your elbow down to your side, rotating your palm in a little.
Reach fully back up to stretch the lat.
exercises.tip: Lean a little toward the working side at the top to deepen the stretch.

exercises.name: Assisted Pull-Up
exercises.description: A pull-up on a counterweight machine, so you can do full reps with less than your body weight.
howTo: Set the assistance, kneel on the pad and grip the bar.
Pull your chest toward the bar.
Lower all the way to a dead hang.
exercises.tip: Use less assistance over time. That's the progression.

exercises.name: Assisted Dip
exercises.description: A dip on a counterweight machine for chest and triceps, building toward bodyweight dips.
howTo: Set the assistance, kneel on the pad and grip the bars.
Lower until your shoulders are slightly below your elbows.
Press back up to straight arms.
exercises.tip: Go only as deep as your shoulders feel good.

exercises.name: Pendulum Squat
exercises.description: A plate-loaded squat on a swinging arc that keeps you upright and loads the quads hard at the bottom.
howTo: Set your shoulders under the pads with your feet in the middle of the platform.
Sit down as deep as you can, letting your knees travel forward.
Drive back up without locking out hard.
exercises.tip: The deep bottom is where it pays off. Use a load you can take all the way down.

exercises.name: Belt Squat
exercises.description: A squat with the load hung from a hip belt, which trains the legs hard without loading your spine.
howTo: Stand on the platform with the belt around your hips.
Squat down between your hips, holding the rails lightly.
Go deep, then drive back up.
exercises.tip: Keep your torso upright. Your hands are for balance, not for pulling.

exercises.name: V-Squat
exercises.description: A plate-loaded machine squat with a set path, between a hack squat and a leg press.
howTo: Set your shoulders under the pads with your feet shoulder width apart on the platform.
Squat down as low as you can control.
Push back up through your mid-foot.
exercises.tip: Keep your hips and back against the pad.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Leg Press
exercises.description: A leg press one leg at a time, to train each side on its own without balance demands.
howTo: Sit in the leg press with one foot in the middle of the platform.
Lower until your knee is deeply bent, keeping your hips on the seat.
Press back up, then switch legs.
exercises.tip: Stop before your lower back lifts off the pad.

exercises.name: High-Foot Leg Press
exercises.description: A leg press with your feet high on the platform to shift the work toward the glutes and adductors.
howTo: Put your feet high and a bit wide on the platform.
Lower until your hips are deeply flexed, keeping your hips on the seat.
Press through your heels to the top.
exercises.tip: Stop before your tailbone curls off the pad.

exercises.name: Nordic Curl
exercises.description: A bodyweight hamstring exercise where you lower your torso forward from kneeling, loading the hamstrings hard as they lengthen.
howTo: Kneel with your ankles anchored under a pad or by a partner.
Keeping your hips straight, lower your body forward as slowly as you can.
Catch yourself with your hands and push back up, or pull back up if you can.
exercises.tip: Start with the slow lowering only. It's very hard, so expect soreness at first.

exercises.name: Glute Kickback Machine
exercises.description: A machine kickback that isolates one glute at a time.
howTo: Set up on the machine with one foot on the plate or pad.
Push your leg back and up by squeezing your glute.
Return slowly without letting your lower back arch.
exercises.tip: Stop when your hip is straight. Going further just bends the lower back.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust Machine
exercises.description: A hip thrust with a padded belt or lever instead of a barbell, so it's quick to set up and comfortable on the hips.
howTo: Sit with your upper back on the pad and the belt or pad across your hips.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips until they're in line with your body.
Squeeze at the top, then lower under control.
exercises.tip: Keep your chin tucked and your ribs down. Finish with your glutes, not your back.

exercises.name: Calf Raise on Leg Press
exercises.description: A calf raise done on the leg press, with the balls of your feet on the bottom edge of the platform.
howTo: Sit in the leg press with only the balls of your feet on the bottom edge of the platform, legs straight.
Let your heels drop toward you for a deep stretch.
Push up onto your toes as far as you can.
exercises.tip: Pause in the stretch for a second each rep. Keep the safeties on.

exercises.name: Ab Crunch Machine
exercises.description: A loaded crunch on a machine, so you can add weight to ab training gradually.
howTo: Sit in the machine with the pads or handles set across your upper chest or shoulders.
Curl your ribs down toward your pelvis.
Return slowly until your abs stretch.
exercises.tip: Think of rounding your spine, not bending at the hips.

exercises.name: 45° Glute Hyperextension
exercises.description: A 45-degree back extension done with a rounded upper back and toes turned out, to make it a glute exercise rather than a lower-back one.
howTo: Set the pad just below your hip bones, with your toes turned out.
Round your upper back slightly and lower until your hamstrings stretch.
Drive your hips into the pad and squeeze your glutes to come up.
exercises.tip: Stop at a straight line. Don't overextend at the top.

exercises.name: Reverse Hyperextension
exercises.description: A hip extension done face down on a reverse hyper, swinging your legs up behind you for the glutes, hamstrings and lower back.
howTo: Lie face down with your hips at the edge of the pad and hold the handles.
Raise your legs back and up until they line up with your body.
Lower under control. Don't swing.
exercises.tip: Let the glutes start the movement, not momentum.

exercises.name: Shrug Machine
exercises.description: A machine shrug that loads the upper traps without your grip giving out first.
howTo: Stand in the machine and grip the handles with your arms straight.
Shrug your shoulders straight up toward your ears.
Lower slowly to a full stretch.
exercises.tip: Pause at the top. Don't roll your shoulders.

exercises.name: Low-to-High Cable Fly
exercises.description: A cable fly from low pulleys up to shoulder height, which biases the upper chest.
howTo: Set both pulleys low and take a handle in each hand.
With a slight elbow bend, sweep your hands up and in to meet at about chin height.
Lower back out slowly to a stretch.
exercises.tip: Lead with the inside of your forearms, not your fists.

exercises.name: High-to-Low Cable Fly
exercises.description: A cable fly from high pulleys down toward your hips, which biases the lower chest.
howTo: Set both pulleys high and step forward into a staggered stance.
Sweep your hands down and together in front of your hips.
Open back up slowly to a stretch.
exercises.tip: Keep your chest up and your shoulders back as your hands meet.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Cable Row
exercises.description: A one-arm seated cable row that lets the lat stretch more than a two-handed row.
howTo: Sit at a low cable and hold one handle with your arm straight.
Row your elbow back toward your hip.
Reach forward and let your shoulder go forward at the end.
exercises.tip: Don't twist your torso to move the weight.

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Cable Row
exercises.description: A seated cable row with a wide overhand grip pulled to the upper chest, for the upper back and rear delts.
howTo: Sit at a low cable holding a wide bar overhand.
Pull the bar to your upper chest with your elbows flared to about 60 degrees.
Return slowly until your shoulder blades spread.
exercises.tip: Stay tall. Don't rock back to finish the rep.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.description: A Romanian deadlift with dumbbells, for the hamstrings and glutes at long length.
howTo: Stand holding dumbbells in front of your thighs with soft knees.
Push your hips back, sliding the weights down your legs, until your hamstrings stretch.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall.
exercises.tip: Keep the dumbbells close to your legs the whole way.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.description: A squat holding one dumbbell at your chest, an easy way to learn deep, upright squatting.
howTo: Hold a dumbbell upright at your chest with both hands.
Sit down between your hips, keeping your elbows inside your knees.
Go deep, then drive back up.
exercises.tip: Use your elbows to nudge your knees out at the bottom.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Reverse Lunge
exercises.description: A reverse lunge with dumbbells, gentler on the knees than a forward lunge.
howTo: Stand holding dumbbells at your sides.
Step one foot back and lower until your back knee nearly touches the floor.
Push through your front foot to return, then switch legs.
exercises.tip: A longer step works the glutes more; a shorter one works the quads more.

exercises.name: Arnold Press
exercises.description: A seated dumbbell press that starts palms in and rotates outward as you press.
howTo: Sit holding dumbbells at chin height with your palms facing you.
Press up, rotating your palms to face forward as you go.
Reverse the rotation as you lower.
exercises.tip: Keep the rotation smooth. It's part of the press, not a separate move.

exercises.name: Cable Y-Raise
exercises.description: A raise from crossed low cables up into a Y shape, for the side delts and lower traps.
howTo: Stand between two low pulleys and cross the cables so each hand holds the opposite handle.
Raise your arms up and out into a Y above shoulder height.
Lower slowly back across your body.
exercises.tip: Use light weight. Your shoulders should do this, not your back.

exercises.name: Concentration Curl
exercises.description: A seated one-arm curl with your elbow braced on your inner thigh, for strict biceps work.
howTo: Sit with your elbow against the inside of your thigh, dumbbell hanging.
Curl the weight up toward your shoulder.
Lower until your arm is straight.
exercises.tip: Keep your upper arm completely still.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Triceps Kickback
exercises.description: A bent-over triceps extension with a dumbbell, hardest at the fully straightened position.
howTo: Hinge forward with your upper arm pinned at your side, elbow bent.
Straighten your arm back until it's fully locked.
Lower slowly to 90 degrees.
exercises.tip: Raise the elbow a little higher than your torso to keep tension on.

exercises.name: JM Press
exercises.description: A hybrid of a close-grip bench press and a skull crusher that lets you load the triceps heavy.
howTo: Lie on a bench holding the bar with a close grip over your chest.
Lower by bending your elbows and letting the bar travel toward your upper chest or chin.
Press back up to straight arms.
exercises.tip: Start light. The hybrid path takes a few sessions to learn.

exercises.name: Sissy Squat
exercises.description: A knee-dominant squat where you lean back as your knees go forward, stretching the quads including the rectus femoris.
howTo: Hold a support with one hand and rise onto the balls of your feet.
Lean back as you bend your knees forward and down, keeping your hips straight.
Go as low as you can control, then push back up.
exercises.tip: Keep a straight line from your knees to your shoulders.

exercises.name: Inverted Row
exercises.description: A bodyweight row under a fixed bar or rings, which you can make harder by lowering the bar or raising your feet.
howTo: Lie under a bar set at about waist height and grip it with your arms straight.
Keep your body straight and pull your chest to the bar.
Lower until your arms are straight.
exercises.tip: Squeeze your glutes so your hips don't sag.

exercises.name: Pike Push-Up
exercises.description: A push-up with your hips raised high so you press at an overhead angle, a bodyweight shoulder press.
howTo: Start in a push-up position and walk your feet in until your hips are high.
Lower your head toward the floor between your hands.
Press back up to straight arms.
exercises.tip: Raise your feet on a box to make it harder.

exercises.name: Weighted Decline Crunch
exercises.description: A crunch on a decline bench holding a plate, for loaded ab work.
howTo: Hook your feet on the decline bench and hold a plate at your chest.
Curl your ribs toward your pelvis to lift your upper back.
Lower slowly until your abs stretch.
exercises.tip: Curl up. Don't swing up by pulling with the hips.

exercises.name: Cable Woodchop
exercises.description: A standing diagonal cable chop for the obliques.
howTo: Set a cable high, stand side-on and grab the handle with both hands.
Pull it down and across your body to the opposite hip, rotating through your torso.
Return slowly along the same diagonal.
exercises.tip: Pivot your back foot so your hips can turn with you.

exercises.name: Pallof Press
exercises.description: An anti-rotation press: you hold a cable straight out in front while it tries to twist you.
howTo: Stand side-on to a cable at chest height, holding the handle at your chest.
Press it straight out until your arms are straight, without letting your torso turn.
Hold briefly, then bring it back.
exercises.tip: Brace like someone is about to push you sideways.

exercises.name: Standing Cable Crunch
exercises.description: A standing rope crunch, a quick loaded ab exercise when the kneeling version isn't comfortable.
howTo: Face away from a high cable, holding the rope by your head.
Crunch down by curling your ribs toward your hips.
Return slowly until your abs stretch.
exercises.tip: Keep your hips still. Only your spine curls.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Y-Raise
exercises.description: A chest-down Y-raise on an incline bench for the lower traps and rear delts.
howTo: Lie face down on a bench at 30 to 45 degrees holding light dumbbells.
Raise your arms up and out into a Y with your thumbs up.
Lower slowly.
exercises.tip: Very light weight. Squeeze the shoulder blades down and back.

exercises.name: Cable Rear Delt Fly
exercises.description: A crossed-cable reverse fly that keeps tension on the rear delts through the full arc.
howTo: Set both pulleys at shoulder height and cross the cables, holding the opposite handle in each hand.
Pull your arms out and back in a wide arc.
Return slowly until your hands cross.
exercises.tip: Pull wide, not back. Think of moving your hands apart.

exercises.name: Overhead Rope Triceps Extension (Low Cable)
exercises.description: An overhead rope extension from a low pulley, facing away, which stretches the long head under load.
howTo: Hold a rope behind your head with your back to a low cable.
Extend your arms overhead until they are straight.
Lower slowly until your elbows are fully bent.
exercises.tip: Keep your elbows close to your head.

exercises.name: Cable Glute Kickback
exercises.description: A standing kickback from a low cable with an ankle strap, isolating one glute.
howTo: Attach an ankle strap and face the stack, holding on for support.
Kick your leg back by squeezing your glute.
Return slowly.
exercises.tip: Lean forward a little so you get a longer range.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Fly
exercises.description: A dumbbell fly on an incline bench, for the upper chest at long length.
howTo: Lie on a bench set at 30 degrees holding dumbbells over your chest, palms facing.
With a slight elbow bend, open your arms wide until your chest stretches.
Bring them back together over your chest.
exercises.tip: Stop the stretch where your shoulders still feel good.

exercises.name: Decline Barbell Bench Press
exercises.description: A barbell bench press on a decline, biasing the lower chest with less front-delt work.
howTo: Hook your legs under the pads on a decline bench and unrack the bar with a medium grip.
Lower it to your lower chest.
Press back up to straight arms.
exercises.tip: Always use a spotter or safeties. Unracking at a decline is awkward.

exercises.name: EZ-Bar Curl
exercises.description: A curl with an angled EZ bar, which is easier on the wrists than a straight bar.
howTo: Stand holding the EZ bar on the angled grips, arms straight.
Curl it up, keeping your elbows by your sides.
Lower to straight arms.
exercises.tip: No swinging. Let the biceps do the lifting.

exercises.name: Spider Curl
exercises.description: A curl lying chest-down on an incline bench with your arms hanging straight down, which loads the biceps hardest at the top.
howTo: Lie face down on an incline bench with dumbbells hanging straight down.
Curl up without letting your elbows move forward.
Lower to straight arms.
exercises.tip: Squeeze hard at the top. That's where this one is hardest.

exercises.name: EZ-Bar Reverse Curl
exercises.description: An overhand-grip curl for the brachioradialis and forearm extensors.
howTo: Hold an EZ bar overhand at shoulder width, arms straight.
Curl it up, keeping your wrists straight.
Lower slowly.
exercises.tip: Use less weight than a regular curl and keep the wrists neutral.

exercises.name: Cable Preacher Curl
exercises.description: A preacher curl with a cable, so the biceps stay loaded at the stretched bottom.
howTo: Set a preacher bench in front of a low cable and take a bar or handle.
Curl up until your forearms are nearly vertical.
Lower to almost straight.
exercises.tip: Control the bottom, where the stretch is.

exercises.name: Standing Single-Leg Curl
exercises.description: A one-leg machine leg curl done standing, for each hamstring on its own.
howTo: Stand in the machine with the pad just above your heel.
Curl your heel toward your glute.
Lower slowly to straight.
exercises.tip: Keep your hips pressed into the pad.

exercises.name: Glute-Ham Raise
exercises.description: A hamstring exercise on a glute-ham bench that trains knee flexion and hip extension together.
howTo: Set your feet against the plate with your knees just behind the pad.
Lower your torso forward under control until your body is horizontal.
Pull yourself back up with your hamstrings.
exercises.tip: Push your toes into the plate to help start the pull.

exercises.name: Barbell Glute Bridge
exercises.description: A hip thrust done with your back on the floor, with a shorter range but quick to set up.
howTo: Lie on the floor with a padded bar across your hips and your knees bent.
Drive through your heels to raise your hips until they're in line with your body.
Squeeze, then lower.
exercises.tip: Tuck your chin and keep your ribs down.

exercises.name: Good Morning
exercises.description: A barbell hinge with the bar on your back, for the hamstrings, glutes and lower back.
howTo: Set the bar on your upper back and stand with soft knees.
Push your hips back and lower your chest until your hamstrings stretch.
Drive your hips forward to stand.
exercises.tip: Start light. The long lever loads the lower back quickly.

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Lateral Raise
exercises.description: A lateral raise done seated, so you can't cheat the weight up with your legs.
howTo: Sit on the end of a bench holding dumbbells at your sides.
Raise them out to shoulder height, leading with your elbows.
Lower slowly.
exercises.tip: Stop at shoulder height and keep your shoulders down.

exercises.name: Deficit Push-Up
exercises.description: A push-up with your hands on plates or handles so your chest can go below hand level for a deeper stretch.
howTo: Set two plates or handles shoulder-width apart and get into a push-up position.
Lower until your chest is below your hands.
Press back up to straight arms.
exercises.tip: Keep your body in a straight line from your head to your heels.

exercises.name: Seated Row Machine (Selectorized)
exercises.description: A selectorized seated row with a chest pad and fixed handles, which keeps the torso still so the mid-back and lats do the work.
howTo: Set the seat so the handles are at about lower-chest height, with your chest on the pad.
Row the handles back until your elbows pass your torso.
Let them go forward until your arms are straight and your shoulder blades spread.
exercises.tip: Keep your chest on the pad. Don't lean back to finish the rep.

exercises.name: High-to-Low Row Machine
exercises.description: A plate-loaded row on a diagonal from above your head down to your waist, sitting between the High Row and a seated row and biased toward the lats.
howTo: Sit with your chest on the pad and reach up and forward for the handles.
Pull down and back on the diagonal until your elbows reach your hips.
Return slowly until your lats stretch.
exercises.tip: Drive your elbows toward your back pockets.

exercises.name: Converging Arc Lat Pulldown
exercises.description: A plate-loaded pulldown whose arms travel in a converging arc, matching the line of the lat fibres and loading the lats hard at the top stretch.
howTo: Sit with your thighs under the pad and reach up for the handles, letting your shoulders rise.
Pull down and in until your elbows are at your sides.
Return slowly all the way to the top stretch.
exercises.tip: The heaviest part is near the top. Don't cut the stretch short.

exercises.name: Standing Lateral Raise Machine
exercises.description: A standing machine lateral raise with handles, which feels like a dumbbell raise on a fixed path with more even tension.
howTo: Stand side-on or facing the machine with the pivot lined up with your shoulders, and take the handles.
Raise your arms out to the sides up to shoulder height.
Lower slowly until the stack nearly touches down.
exercises.tip: Gripping handles lets the traps help more than elbow pads do, so keep your shoulders down.

exercises.name: Converging Smith Bench Press
exercises.description: A Smith bench press on a machine whose rails angle inward, so the bar travels up and slightly toward your face like a free bench, with a bit more chest focus.
howTo: Lie on the bench so the bar lines up with your mid-chest at the bottom.
Unrack, then lower under control to your chest.
Press up along the angled path to straight arms.
exercises.tip: Set the safeties just above your chest before you start.

exercises.name: Converging Smith Incline Press
exercises.description: An incline Smith press on angled rails that move the bar up and back over the shoulders, for the upper chest.
howTo: Set an incline bench at 30 to 45 degrees so the bar meets your upper chest.
Lower under control to your upper chest.
Press up along the angled path.
exercises.tip: Keep your shoulder blades back and your chest high.

exercises.name: Converging Smith Shoulder Press
exercises.description: A seated overhead press on angled Smith rails that carry the bar slightly back over your head, a natural pressing path with no balance demand.
howTo: Sit on an upright bench with the bar at about chin height.
Press up along the path until your arms are straight.
Lower back to chin height.
exercises.tip: Keep your back on the pad. Don't arch to finish the rep.

exercises.name: Pulldown Machine (Selectorized)
exercises.description: A selectorized lever pulldown with fixed handles, with a smoother, more stable path than a cable bar.
howTo: Sit with your thighs under the pad and take the handles.
Pull down until your elbows are at your sides.
Return slowly to straight arms.
exercises.tip: Keep your chest up and pull with your elbows.

exercises.name: Plate-Loaded Chest-Supported Row
exercises.description: A plate-loaded chest-supported row with a long lever, which loads hardest near full contraction and suits heavy upper-back work.
howTo: Set the chest pad so you can reach the handles with straight arms.
Row the handles back, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower until your arms are straight and your shoulder blades spread.
exercises.tip: Pause at the top for a second. The lever makes that position hardest.

exercises.name: Rotary Torso Machine
exercises.description: A seated machine that rotates your torso against resistance, for direct oblique work.
howTo: Sit with your knees locked in and your chest against the pads.
Rotate your torso to one side through a comfortable range.
Return slowly, then do the other side.
exercises.tip: Move slowly. Don't let the weight swing you back.

exercises.name: Standing Cable Hip Adduction
exercises.description: A standing cable adduction with an ankle strap, which trains each adductor on its own and lets you go through a long range.
howTo: Attach the strap to your inside ankle and stand side-on to a low cable.
Sweep the leg across in front of the other one.
Return slowly as far as is comfortable.
exercises.tip: Stand tall and hold on. Don't lean into it.

exercises.name: Horizontal Leg Press
exercises.description: A seated selectorized leg press that pushes straight out. It's usually lighter and easier on the lower back than a 45-degree sled, but you can't go quite as deep.
howTo: Sit with your back flat on the pad and your feet shoulder width on the platform.
Bend your knees toward your chest as far as your hips allow.
Press out until your legs are almost straight.
exercises.tip: Keep your hips down on the seat at the bottom.

exercises.name: Reverse Hack Squat
exercises.description: A hack squat done facing the pad with your hips pushed back. It shifts the work from the quads toward the glutes and hamstrings.
howTo: Face the machine with your chest on the back pad and your shoulders under the pads.
Push your hips back and squat down until your hips are deeply flexed.
Drive back up through your heels.
exercises.tip: Let your hips travel back, not just down.

exercises.name: Kneeling Leg Curl
exercises.description: A one-leg curl kneeling on a pad with your hip slightly bent, partway between a lying and a seated curl.
howTo: Kneel on the pad with the roller just above one heel and your forearms on the support.
Curl your heel toward your glute.
Lower slowly to straight.
exercises.tip: Keep your hips square on the pad.

exercises.name: Smith Squat (Feet Forward)
exercises.description: A Smith squat with your feet set ahead of the bar, so you can sit back and down. Compared with the standard Smith squat, it moves some of the work to the glutes.
howTo: Set the bar on your upper back and put your feet about a foot in front of it.
Sit down and slightly back until your thighs are at least parallel.
Drive up through your whole foot.
exercises.tip: Wider and further forward means more glutes. Narrower and under the bar means more quads.

exercises.name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
exercises.description: A two-dumbbell row lying face down on an incline bench, needing no machine and putting no load on the lower back.
howTo: Lie chest-down on a bench at about 30 degrees with dumbbells hanging.
Row both dumbbells up until your elbows pass your torso.
Lower to a full reach.
exercises.tip: Keep your chest on the bench. Don't lift it to cheat.

exercises.name: Seal Row
exercises.description: A barbell row lying face down on a high flat bench, so the row is strict and your lower back is completely out of it.
howTo: Lie face down on a high bench with the barbell underneath and your arms straight.
Row the bar up to the underside of the bench.
Lower to a full stretch.
exercises.tip: Use a cambered bar or blocks if the bench is too low for a full range.

exercises.name: Yates Row
exercises.description: An underhand barbell row with your torso about 30 degrees forward of upright, which lets you row heavy and brings in more lats and biceps.
howTo: Hold the bar underhand at shoulder width and hinge to about 30 degrees.
Row it to your lower stomach, driving your elbows back.
Lower under control to straight arms.
exercises.tip: Keep the torso angle fixed. Don't stand up into each rep.

exercises.name: Rack Pull
exercises.description: A deadlift from pins at about knee height that trains heavy lockouts for the back, traps and glutes.
howTo: Set the bar on pins just below or at your knees and grip it just outside your legs.
Brace, then drive your hips forward to stand tall.
Lower back to the pins under control.
exercises.tip: Don't lean back at the top. Stand tall and stop.

exercises.name: Trap-Bar Deadlift
exercises.description: A deadlift inside a hexagonal bar with neutral handles, which keeps you more upright and shares the work between the quads and hips.
howTo: Stand in the centre of the bar and grip the handles.
Sit your hips down until your shoulders are over the handles, then brace.
Drive the floor away and stand tall.
Lower by pushing your hips back.
exercises.tip: Use the high handles to start if your mobility is limited.

exercises.name: Captain's Chair Knee Raise
exercises.description: A knee raise with your forearms on a captain's chair, an easier step toward the hanging leg raise.
howTo: Support yourself on the chair's forearm pads with your back against the pad.
Raise your knees toward your chest, curling your pelvis up at the top.
Lower slowly to straight legs.
exercises.tip: Curling the pelvis is what works the abs. Just lifting the knees mostly works the hip flexors.

exercises.name: Back Extension Machine (Selectorized)
exercises.description: A seated selectorized back extension that trains the lower back directly with very little load on the hips.
howTo: Sit with the pad across your upper back and your feet braced.
Extend your spine back against the pad.
Return slowly forward.
exercises.tip: Move through a comfortable range. Don't snap into extension.

exercises.name: Reverse Wrist Curl
exercises.description: A palms-down wrist curl for the forearm extensors, the opposite side from a normal wrist curl.
howTo: Rest your forearms on a bench with your palms facing down and dumbbells in your hands.
Raise the backs of your hands toward you.
Lower slowly.
exercises.tip: Light weight and full range. The extensors are small muscles.

exercises.name: Farmer Carry
exercises.description: A heavy carry with a dumbbell or handle in each hand, for grip, upper traps and trunk stiffness.
howTo: Deadlift a heavy dumbbell or handle in each hand and stand tall.
Walk with short, quick steps for a set distance or time.
Set the weights down with a flat back.
exercises.tip: Shoulders down and back, ribs down. Don't let the weights pull you into a slouch.
